text:
maria.chen: heads up — we saw a ~3% jump of canary traffic being routed to baseline during the 20:00 UTC TTL rollover window. looks like sticky cookie expired and fallback path is doing a different hash calc

samir.kapoor: can you paste the rollout config and an example request id?

maria.chen: cfg snippet: ```
routes:
  canary:
    weight: 5
    sticky:
      type: cookie
      name: rwd_aff
      ttl: 3600
    fallback: header-hash
```

maria.chen: example req-id: r-9a1f2c4d, observed assignment: canary -> baseline after TTL expiry

liam: curious — fallback header-hash is configured to use `x-session` header, right? we normalize UA elsewhere, maybe header normalization order differs after cookie expiry

maria.chen: yes fallback uses x-session then x-client-id. logs show on expiry path we got `x-session` missing and used `x-client-id` which has different entropy distribution

jordan_p: quick repro idea: reduce ttl to 30s on staging and run load with mix of clients to see churn pattern

maria.chen: did that, reproduced. fwiw the hash func for header-hash changed last month to include lowercasing, but cookie-hash uses raw value. mismatch causes bucket flip when fallback used

samir.kapoor: ah — two issues then: (1) inconsistent normalization between cookie and header hash, (2) header fallback uses a lower-entropy header priority order. both increase flip probability across small weights

liam: proposed short fix: make header-hash use the same normalization pipeline as cookie-hash (lowercase + trim) and add a stable salt per-route so hash(space) is stable across code paths

jordan_p: also add telemetry: emit 'routing-path' tag (cookie|fallback-header|fallback-hash) in trace so we can count TTL-triggered flips easily

maria.chen: good. i'm worried about rollout UX — ops saw this as a canary leak and rolled back manually. can console show 'transient sticky expiry' warning during rollouts?

samir.kapoor: yes, we can add a rollout heuristic: if sticky is cookie-based and TTL < 24h, surface 'TTL expiry may cause bucket reassignments' with a link to docs. small change in UI and docs. low risk

rollout-bot: [notice] Canary deploy 2026-03-19T20:00 started for service api-frontend, id=canary-2026-03-19-2000

ops-bot: alert: routing-leak-rate > 1% for canary on prod-east at 2026-03-19T20:01

liam: long term: prefer unified hashing library. short term: patch normalization + add salt + telemetry. can someone own the patch?

maria.chen: i'll open the PR for normalization + telemetry, assign to samir for review. will also put a follow-up for console UX

samir.kapoor: ack. I'll also add a quick guard: if fallback header-hash bucket weight diverges >0.5% from intended during a rollout window, autoset fallback to deterministic-seed (no header fallback) for 5m and alert

jordan_p: yes — that guard would prevent noisy flips during TTL churn windows

maria.chen: thanks all. created issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-5421 and a staging run scheduled at 2026-03-20T02:00 UTC

liam: ping @maria.chen when PR is ready and i'll run the canary with ttl=30s test

maria.chen: will do :thumbsup:
